title: Lattice deploy cue sheet and release microjournal
content:
Purpose: Compact cue-sheet and micro-journal for a staggered, region-aware lattice deploy. This is a working draft — notes to self + shift handoff content included.

Summary:
- Goal: Ship v2 routing + batcher improvements with minimal customer impact. Enforce latency SLO (p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms) while enabling autoscale knob.
- Window: 2026-05-18 08:00–14:00 PT (6 hour window with optional rollback). Primary regions: us-west1, eu-west2, ap-northeast1.
- Approach: Micro-cohort canaries per region -> 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% over 3 phases with short dwell checks. Fallback targets: previous runtime image & model-variant -v1.3.

Quick-rollout cadence (times are offsets from window start):
- T+00:00 (08:00 PT): Preflight smoke and cert checks (runbook preflight-* queries)
- T+00:10: Canary group A (service instances in us-west1) -> route 3% traffic -> 10 requests/sec sampling
- T+00:25: Observe 15m: latency p95, error rate, ratio of fallback responses
- T+00:45: If green, advance Canary B (eu-west2) -> route 3% -> parallel observe
- T+01:30: If both green -> expand to 30% in each region (T+1:30) for 25m
- T+02:00: Roll to 80% global; quick smoke; final 1 hr soak before 100%
- T+03:15: Final ramp to 100% if no regression. Hold for 60m.

Operator checklist (copied to shift binder):
- Pre-window (owner: Morgan):
  - confirm build tag present in /images (service:v2026-05-rc3) and checksum matches CI
  - post release note draft to #releases with TL;DR and rollback plan
  - ensure on-call SRE and Observability engineers are paged (see slack thread: #ops-launch-2431)
  - schedule short notice to customer-success for high-volume customers
- At T+00:00 (owner: Jordan):
  - run `preflight/smoke.sh` against staging-shadow endpoints
  - verify DB migrations (none for this release) and cached config flags
- Canary rollout steps (owner: Priya):
  - bump traffic percentages via router policy: route-key lattice-canary -> 3% per region
  - verify health endpoints respond (200s) and kv-cache hit-rate remains > 75%
- Observability & gating (owner: Diego):
  - run provided queries: latency_p50_p95(), error_rate_by_route(), kvcache_miss() (see linked query ids)
  - verify no increase > 2x baseline for 95th percentile latency and error rate < 0.5% absolute increase

Telemetry snapshot queries (copy into observability):
- Baseline set (T-24h):
  - latency.summary{route:lattice} by region -> p50/p95
  - errors.count{route:lattice,code:5xx} / requests.count{route:lattice}
  - model-fallback.count / requests.count by region
- Live checks:
  - p95_delta = p95_now / p95_baseline -> alert if > 1.9
  - error_delta = (errs_now - errs_baseline) / requests_now -> alert if > 0.005
  - kv_miss_change absolute delta > 0.12 -> deeper inspection

Gating rules (fast fail thresholds):
- Immediate rollback trigger (auto or manual):
  - sustained error rate > 2% for 5 mins OR
  - p95 latency > 500ms for 5 mins OR
  - model-fallback rate > 3% over 10m OR
  - a single SEV impacting multiple customers (pager)
- Soft hold (requires triage and explicit thumbs-up):
  - p95 latency increased 20–50% or error rate increased 0.5–2% -> pause rollout and collect traces; escalate if no mitigation in 20m

Rollback quick commands (operator cheat):
- rollback to image: `router rollback --to previous-image --reason "p95 regression"`
- throttle traffic: `route scale --weight lattice:50%` (sightline fallback)
- emergency kill-switch: feature-flag "lattice.enable" -> set=false (propagates in 10s)

Release notes (draft) — to be posted after final green:
- Summary: "Routing runtime improvements: v2026-05-rc3 introduces the lattice batcher and cost-aware routing optimizations, improving throughput for long-context requests and reducing tail latency by ~15% in internal tests."
- Notable changes: batcher v2, kv-cache eviction tuning, router policy DSL extensions (support weight-by-region).
- Migration notes: No customer action required. If you pinned endpoints, update to the new variant via console or API by 2026-06-01 to pick up cost improvements.
- Known issues: Early RC showed an interaction with some GPU-quantized model variants causing elevated fallback rates. Mitigation: we limit model-variant selection in the rollout.

Operational chores (post-100%):
- Collect 3x hourly telemetry dumps for the next 6 hours (owner: Diego)
- Run automated alert audit: verify no paging storms and alert noise is within expected limits
- Postmortem starter: if any gate triggered, start page in JIRA RELEASING-xxx and fill the microjournal section below

Micro-journal (shift notes and observations) — fill during window:
- [T+00:12] Jordan: Canary A brought up; small spike in small-request latency (p95 +12%). Observed increased queue depth on batcher nodes.
- [T+00:20] Priya: Increased batcher concurrency cap by +10% on canary nodes; tail came down to +4% over baseline. Continue observe.
- [T+00:46] Diego: Canary B shows similar pattern; kv_miss rose from 18% -> 29% on eu-west2. Decided to pause expansion and investigate cache warming strategy.
- [T+01:05] Morgan: Decided to proceed with limited expansion to 30% but restricted to instances with warmed cache tag.

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self):
- Should we include a lightweight warmup job to pre-populate KV cache in the next rollout? (Pros: smoother tails; Cons: extra load on DB)
- Add an observability dashboard tile for batcher queue length per-region (low priority backlog).
- Coordinate with CS for customers using pinned-variants who may see slightly higher latency during first 24h. Draft customer note.

Pointers / links for handoff:
- CI artifact: gh/actions/builds/2431 -> image:v2026-05-rc3
- Observation queries: confluence:obs-queries/lattice-2026
- Slack channel: #ops-launch-2431 (watch pinned messages)

Appendix — quick snippets and commands:
- smoke script: `scripts/smoke/lattice-preflight.sh --tag v2026-05-rc3`
- debug trace command: `tracer collect --route lattice --duration 120s --out traces.tgz`
- simple traffic throttle: `router set-weight --route lattice --weight 10% --region eu-west2`

End notes: This doc is intentionally compact to live in the shift binder. Keep the micro-journal chronological and terse. After release, convert to a full postmortem if any gate triggered.

-- Morgan (on-call release lead)
